rated_messages.input_message: Write down why you want to stop smoking to resist a craving. Remember, trying something to beat the urge is always better than doing nothing. Each time you resist a cig, you're one step closer to being tobacco-free.

Reduce your stress by using your next break to list four things that have gone well so far today. It might feel like a bit of effort, but doing this will help your mind to refocus, and help you to feel calmer.
One way to combat any urges is to keep your mouth busy - some people find that chewing sugar free gum, mints, or even a pen can be a good alternative.
Keep picturing yourself getting home later today knowing that you've gained a smoke-free day. It's nearly a reality!
A funny thing about people is that we tend to believe what we tell ourselves. So make sure that whatever else happens today, tell yourself "I can, and I will stick to not smoking!"
Instead of smoking, keep your fingers busy by scrolling through your phone.

Add the phrase “I’m having the thought that…” in front of your unhelpful thoughts. For example, “I’m having the thought that I need a cigarette.” Your thoughts are not always true or helpful! They are just thoughts.
Step back from what is stressful by taking 10 slow breaths. Count them as you go and notice your breath. If you get distracted, keep starting over until you get to 10.

Think of urges as loud construction noises. Sometimes there's nothing you can do except agree that it's annoying. If you fight it, you feel more irritated, right? Let your urge be there until it passes on its own.
This craving is just an event. A game. It will pass. The game gets easier the more you let your urge pass without smoking. But, it gets harder every time you give in to the urge and smoke.
